ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, two triangular plates of the same size containing $45^\circ$, triangular plate ACF and triangular plate CFB are placed as shown. Point D is on side AC, and point E is on side BC, with $\angle CFE=13^\circ$ and $\angle CFD=32^\circ$. What is the measure of $\angle DEC$ in degrees?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:}

Construct $FH \perp FE$, intersecting $AC$ at point $H$.\\
$\because$ $\angle AFC=\angle EFH=90^\circ$\\
Also, $\because$ $\angle AFC=\angle AFH+\angle CFH$ and $\angle HFE=\angle CFE+\angle CFH$\\
$\therefore$ $\angle AFH=\angle CFE=13^\circ$\\
$\because$ $\angle A=\angle FCE=45^\circ$ and $FA=CF$\\
$\therefore$ $\triangle FAH\cong \triangle FCE$ (ASA)\\
$\therefore$ $FH=FE$\\
$\because$ $\angle DFE=\angle DFC+\angle EFC=32^\circ+13^\circ=45^\circ$\\
$\because$ $\angle DFH=\angle HFE-\angle DFE=90^\circ-45^\circ=45^\circ$\\
$\therefore$ $\angle DFE=\angle DFH$\\
Also, $\because$ $DF=DF$\\
$\therefore$ $\triangle HDF\cong \triangle EDF$ (SAS)\\
$\therefore$ $\angle DHF=\angle DEF$\\
$\because$ $\angle DHF=\angle A+\angle HFA=45^\circ+13^\circ=58^\circ$\\
$\therefore$ $\angle DEF=58^\circ$\\
$\because$ $\angle CFE+\angle CEF+\angle FCE=180^\circ$\\
$\therefore$ $\angle CEF=180^\circ-\angle CFE-\angle FCE=180^\circ-13^\circ-45^\circ=122^\circ$\\
$\therefore$ $\angle DEC=\angle CEF-\angle DEF=122^\circ-58^\circ=\boxed{64^\circ}$

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, two triangular plates of the same size containing $45^\circ$, triangular plate ACF and triangular plate CFB are placed as shown. Point D is on side AC, and point E is on side BC, with $\angle CFE=13^\circ$ and $\angle CFD=32^\circ$. What is the measure of $\angle DEC$ in degrees?
raw_record.answer:
\textbf{Solution:}

Construct $FH \perp FE$, intersecting $AC$ at point $H$.\\
$\because$ $\angle AFC=\angle EFH=90^\circ$\\
Also, $\because$ $\angle AFC=\angle AFH+\angle CFH$ and $\angle HFE=\angle CFE+\angle CFH$\\
$\therefore$ $\angle AFH=\angle CFE=13^\circ$\\
$\because$ $\angle A=\angle FCE=45^\circ$ and $FA=CF$\\
$\therefore$ $\triangle FAH\cong \triangle FCE$ (ASA)\\
$\therefore$ $FH=FE$\\
$\because$ $\angle DFE=\angle DFC+\angle EFC=32^\circ+13^\circ=45^\circ$\\
$\because$ $\angle DFH=\angle HFE-\angle DFE=90^\circ-45^\circ=45^\circ$\\
$\therefore$ $\angle DFE=\angle DFH$\\
Also, $\because$ $DF=DF$\\
$\therefore$ $\triangle HDF\cong \triangle EDF$ (SAS)\\
$\therefore$ $\angle DHF=\angle DEF$\\
$\because$ $\angle DHF=\angle A+\angle HFA=45^\circ+13^\circ=58^\circ$\\
$\therefore$ $\angle DEF=58^\circ$\\
$\because$ $\angle CFE+\angle CEF+\angle FCE=180^\circ$\\
$\therefore$ $\angle CEF=180^\circ-\angle CFE-\angle FCE=180^\circ-13^\circ-45^\circ=122^\circ$\\
$\therefore$ $\angle DEC=\angle CEF-\angle DEF=122^\circ-58^\circ=\boxed{64^\circ}$
raw_record.final_cot: Image description: The diagram shows A, F, B on a horizontal line, with C above F. Segments AC and BC form two triangular plates ACF and CFB sharing CF. Point D is marked on AC, point E is marked on BC, and the segments FD, FE, and DE are drawn. Reasoning: Since the two plates are congruent 45-45-90 triangles, we have ∠AFC = 90°, ∠A = 45°, ∠FCE = 45°, and AF = CF. From the problem, ∠CFE = 13° and ∠CFD = 32°. Construct H on AC such that FH ⟂ FE. Then ∠HFE = 90°, and also ∠AFC = 90°. Comparing ∠AFC = ∠AFH + ∠CFH with ∠HFE = ∠CFE + ∠CFH gives ∠AFH = ∠CFE = 13°. In triangles FAH and FCE, AF = CF, ∠FAH = ∠FCE = 45°, and ∠AFH = ∠CFE = 13°, so △FAH ≅ △FCE by ASA. Hence FH = FE. Next, ∠DFE = ∠DFC + ∠CFE = 32° + 13° = 45°. Since ∠HFE = 90°, ∠DFH = 90° − 45° = 45°. Thus ∠DFH = ∠DFE. With DF common and FH = FE, triangles HDF and EDF are congruent by SAS. Therefore ∠DHF = ∠DEF. Now ∠DHF = ∠A + ∠AFH = 45° + 13° = 58°, so ∠DEF = 58°. In triangle CFE, ∠CEF = 180° − ∠CFE − ∠FCE = 180° − 13° − 45° = 122°. Finally, ∠DEC = ∠CEF − ∠DEF = 122° − 58° = 64°.
